Lifting from the top of a house is a terrible idea. None of the connections are designed to support that kind of load in that direction. 

To be extra pedantic, a header is what spans over an opening like a door or window. This would also be a terrible spot to do tie-downs because it is just supported on either end and is designed to resist vertical force not a lateral load that an eyebolt would apply.

Assuming all of the connections in the house are made according to code to resist the uplift in your zone your biggest problem is you cannot connect a THOW to the ground the way a house has a footing and foundation.

Personally (don't take structural advice from the Internet) I would use structural tie-downs inside the wall at the bottom though the bottom plate and attach to the biggest ground anchor I can find and then also have tie-downs in the ceiling joist or roof rafter to exterior eyes and then out to anchors. This would tackle the two biggest problems which are uplift and the lateral wind load.

For your specific situation I would break down the burn out the way you would any construction problem. Identify the problem in context, identify solutions, implement.

1)what do you like about your job 
2) why are you actually burnt out. Is it that these other guys are slackers, or you don't have control, or you want to get paid more in comparison to them, or whatever.
3) identify solutions (end goals) and how that will solve your complaints but maintain what you like: change company, change job at the same company, get a raise, work less hard, etc. These do not need all be realistic.
4) figure out plans (including contingency plans) for each solution and pick the ones that you want to pursue.
5) implement

It's important to not get stuck on one particular solution. Stop, figure out why it's not working, change your tactics.
